gameForms.survival: supports relational challenge, FailureAssessment, optional RecoveryTransitionSet and scoped mastery

gameForms.masteryPressure: memorized solution performance does not establish transfer to structurally transformed puzzles
gameForms.survival: supports condition/history binding and probe-scoped mastery; weakens controllability/retry as universal learning-opportunity requirements

gameForms.survival: supports criterion-relative failure and capability-expression guards

gameForms.survival: strong FailureAssessment + RecoveryTransitionSet boundary; death/terminality identities rejected

gameForms.survival: proves challenge/mastery contracts must be evaluation-authority-relative and recovery is optional, not universal

crossFormLaws: Difficulty/Challenge is not an intrinsic scalar property of content
Challenge claim requires evaluation criterion, attribution target and condition/horizon scope
Outcome probability, capability threshold/discrimination, risk and recovery cost are distinct projections
Failure requires evaluation scope/horizon and can be local without being pursuit-terminal
RecoveryTransitionSet is optional and relevant only where post-outcome continuation/recovery structure exists
LearningOpportunity does not require failure, cheap retry, or direct control of the observed variable by identity
Mastery is a scoped claim over SkillProfile/evidence, not a Game state boolean
Continuous/open-ended mastery does not require terminal completion
Synthetic structural mastery evidence != Human mastery/experience by identity
Current rules/evaluation/provenance are part of any challenge/failure/mastery claim

externalPressure.pressure: expertise indicators in StarCraft telemetry vary in importance across skill levels and total score can hide different strategies/skill components; supports non-scalar mastery evidence
performance under a major StarCraft domain/version change provides direct within-expertise transfer pressure; mastery evidence must remain condition/transformation scoped

13 participants with upper-limb impairments used human cooperation and partial automation in Rocket League; both reduced control burden while modalities differed and action misattribution/confusion occurred, directly supporting shared-control attribution boundaries

foundationReopen.reason: all cross-form pressures are representable through existing evaluation, authority/provenance, state/transition/history and frozen GDF1 skill/control coordinates; no new semantic primitive is forced.
